metric.definition: The share of provisioned compute doing real work, measured over time rather than at peak.

reading.body:
Server utilization rate is the share of provisioned compute doing real work, measured over time rather than at peak, and it is the denominator that makes every data center efficiency metric honest.

Idle servers burn power, licenses, and depreciation while producing nothing. Fleet utilization is where the money hides in most enterprise estates, so this metric turns raw provisioned capacity into a measure of actual compute output. Low utilization means power is consumed without corresponding work, which matters wherever power is a constrained input.

The metric is tracked under operations and sits beside stranded power and space per cabinet and floor loading limits, all within capacity and server use. That grouping treats utilization as one of several physical and operational constraints, not a standalone score. The definition measures over time rather than at peak, so it can smooth over short bursts of contention or idleness, and it does not explain why servers are idle or whether the work being done is valuable.
